task.description:
Re-gate ADHOC-20260821-002 after rework iteration 1. Your own step-02 gate FAILed the first pass with a BLOCKER (G1) and six further items; DOC-UPDATER reports all seven closed in commit 808e2e1 (135 insertions, 19 deletions across six files). Review `git show 808e2e1`, and `git diff b13a523~1..HEAD -- <the six files>` if you want the cumulative view.

**Re-derive closure from the files themselves.** Reading step-03-rework.json's result and confirming it back is not validation. You wrote the gaps; you are the right role to judge whether they are actually closed, and the wrong one to take a producer's word for it.

PARTICULAR ATTENTION TO THREE THINGS:

  1. **G1 was the BLOCKER and its test is mechanical, not stylistic.** The defect was a precedence inversion: a rank-3 workflow doc made the mutant run mandatory while the rank-2 role file made it discretionary. Check the fix by ASKING THE PRECEDENCE QUESTION AGAIN rather than by reading the new prose approvingly: with both files as they now stand, does an agent applying core-directives' Instruction Precedence chain reach MANDATORY from either direction? A partial fix here — e.g. the role file now strict but some other rank-1/rank-2 source still permissive — leaves the original defect in place with better wording on top. Sweep for any OTHER rank-1 or rank-2 source (role files under .claude/agents/, other instruction files) that speaks to fail-first or mutation testing and could still read as permissive.

  2. **DOC-UPDATER raised a NEW consequence of its own G3 fix, and it is the kind of finding this gate exists to catch.** GIT_MERGE.md step 7's PR body template still prints a bare `mix test: PASS`. After G3 redefined 'green' as 'no failure attributable to this branch', an agent with a correctly-attributed non-zero failure count now writes PASS on the PR next to a run that reported failures, with no attribution recorded anywhere a later reader would see it. It did not fix this — correctly, since it is a template rather than a rule and was outside the seven items. **Rule on it.** Is it a real defect introduced by this run's own change, and if so is it in scope to fix now or a follow-up? Note the asymmetry that makes it worth taking seriously: the PR body is the one artefact a human is most likely to read, and 'PASS' next to an unstated failure count is precisely the shape core-directives' 'Never Call a Red Pipeline OK Without a Source' forbids.

  3. **Confirm the rework did not weaken anything.** This pass has 19 deletions where the first had none. DOC-UPDATER reports each maps to a site an item required amending. Verify that independently and name any deletion that is not accounted for by one of G1..G7.

Also re-check the two things you passed last time that the rework touched — R1's text (changed by G4, G5, G7) and R3's (changed by G1, G2) — for whether the amendments introduced any new ambiguity or contradiction. And confirm G7's third attribution route did not accidentally make the rule permissive: it must require a MEASUREMENT of the mechanism, so that the route is harder to satisfy than the two it supplements, not an escape hatch from them.

Do NOT rewrite the docs. PASS or FAIL, and a FAIL names each gap and the change that closes it. If you PASS, say explicitly whether item 2 above is a follow-up ORCH should file.
acceptance_criteria: G1..G7 each given an individual closed/not-closed verdict re-derived from the files, not from the producer's report

G1 specifically re-tested by re-asking the precedence question against the current text of both files, plus a sweep for any other rank-1/rank-2 source that could still read as permissive on fail-first or mutation testing
An explicit ruling on the PR-body-template finding: real defect or not, in scope now or a follow-up, with reasoning
All 19 deletions accounted for against G1..G7, with any unaccounted deletion named
R1's and R3's amended text re-checked for new ambiguity or contradiction introduced by the rework
G7's third route confirmed to require a measurement rather than functioning as an escape hatch from the other two
PASS or FAIL stated, with any FAIL naming each gap and its closing change
No file outside handoffs/ is modified by this step

result.summary:
ALL SEVEN GAPS G1-G7 ARE CLOSED, re-derived from the files rather than from step-03's report. The rework is sound and nothing in it is wrong. The FAIL is narrow and is on ONE new item -- G8, the GIT_MERGE.md step 7 PR body template -- which DOC-UPDATER itself raised and correctly declined to fix, and which this gate rules is a real defect made systematic by this run's own G3 change, in scope now rather than as a follow-up. b13a523 and 808e2e1 are both sound and neither should be reverted; the rework is one template line plus a pointer.

PER-GAP VERDICTS, RE-DERIVED FROM THE FILES.

G1 (BLOCKER) -- CLOSED. Re-tested MECHANICALLY by re-asking the precedence question against both files as they now stand, not by reading the new prose. Rank 2, `.claude/agents/test-design-validator.md` lines 27-45: the cheapness parenthetical is gone from line 27 ('confirm the spec states, and verify yourself'), and lines 30-40 add 'you MUST additionally apply at least one of TEST-DESIGNER's reported mutants to the shipped logic yourself, run the suite, and quote your own measured counts. This is mandatory -- it is not subject to a cheapness test, and it is not satisfied by reading TEST-DESIGNER's reported counts.' Rank 3, WF-03 lines 118-120: 'TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR must independently APPLY at least one of the reported mutants and run it.' Both directions of the chain now terminate at MANDATORY, and rank 2 is now at least as strict as rank 3, so first-match-wins no longer defeats the rule. The inversion is gone, not papered over.

SWEEP FOR OTHER RANK-1/RANK-2 PERMISSIVE SOURCES (this gate's AC2). `grep -rniE 'mutant|mutat|fail.?first|pre-fix|failed against|cheap|actually fail' .claude/agents/ docs/agents/instructions/ docs/agents/shared/ docs/agents/protocols/ CLAUDE.md` returns exactly three files that speak to fail-first or mutation: test-design-validator.md (now strict), test-designer.md line 49-51, and TASK_QUEUE.md (unrelated sense of 'mutate'). No rank-1 source exists to check (handoff task blocks are per-run). test-designer.md is the only remaining rank-2 text on the subject and it is NOT permissive: 'the test must be shown to fail against the pre-fix code and pass against the fix -- state this explicitly in the spec, and actually verify it rather than asserting it.' It states a necessary condition, never a sufficient one, and carries no cheapness or discretion qualifier -- so it does not conflict with WF-03's rank-3 mandate and precedence does not fire. It is however SILENT on the non-existence carve-out, which is a discoverability gap rather than an inversion; recorded as G9, non-gating, with the reasoning for that distinction stated there. R3 is genuinely in force.

G2 (MAJOR) -- CLOSED. WF-03 lines 134-153 open 'A mutant is a TEMPORARY PROBE. Leaving one in the tree is a step failure', name the scope conflict being resolved ('a gate step is otherwise bound by no file outside handoffs/ is modified by this step'), and give both techniques concretely: preferred throwaway `git worktree`; or in-place `git checkout -- <path>` with the revert VERIFIED by `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` empty AND the test file re-running green, both quoted in result.summary. The WF03-ISS0106-20260821 precedent is cited with the correct framing -- 'it is stated here so it no longer depends on a per-run handoff remembering to ask', which is precisely the defect G2 named. The same two-technique rule is mirrored at test-design-validator.md lines 42-45 so it travels with the rank-2 mandate rather than being reachable only via WF-03. Verified independently.

G3 (MAJOR) -- CLOSED, in the shape this gate specified, all three parts. (a) Step 5d, GIT_MERGE.md lines 146-158: a warning block after `mix test` requiring structural attribution per core-directives, stating 'Green at this step means NO FAILURE ATTRIBUTABLE TO THIS BRANCH, not zero failures', forbidding count comparison by name, routing structurally-cleared failures to file-and-forward, and making unattributed blocking; the terminator is correctly re-worded to 'If FAIL (i.e. at least one failure is attributable to this branch, or is unattributed)'. (b) Precondition, lines 30-38: a 'What reported green means here' paragraph making the same redefinition, naming the standing 13-15, and stating that 'zero failures' would make the precondition unsatisfiable. Both point at R1's canonical home and explicitly do not restate it -- 'read it there; it is not restated here' -- which is the right shape. (c) R2 pointer, lines 55-59: exactly one addition under step 2, reusing that step's existing shared-checkout rationale, 'stage by explicit filename only (already required above) and push only your own commits; see ORCHESTRATOR.md 7.1'. `git push origin <sha>:main` is correctly NOT restated. Confirmed by reading the current file, not the diff alone.

G4 (MINOR) -- CLOSED, both directions. core-directives line 243-245 inserts into Unblock-Everything's Scope boundary: 'for a test failure, which side of this line it falls on is decided by Failure Attribution Is Structural, Never By Count-Matching below, not by judgement'. R1 line 314-318 carries the reciprocal pointer naming the Scope boundary and which side each verdict lands on. See G11 for a non-gating readability nit in how the insertion sits inside the host sentence.

G5 (MINOR) -- CLOSED. WF-02 Step 4 item 3 now reads 'called out AS SUCH and REPORTED FOR FILING per ISSUE_QUEUE.md ... You report the finding; you do NOT call the queue or gh yourself. Only ORCH allocates issue ids (ISSUE_QUEUE.md, amended 2026-08-21)', with the id-collision rationale named so a future agent can tell why the rule exists. Mirrored into WF-04's item 3. Checked against `docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md` lines 31 and 49-50 -- the new wording matches that protocol exactly. One residual instance of the same defect survives in core-directives and is recorded as G10, non-gating because precedence resolves it correctly there (protocols are rank 4, core-directives rank 5) rather than invertedly as in G1.

G6 (MINOR) -- CLOSED. WF-04 Step 1's six-line prose paragraph is replaced by the same fenced four-point checklist as WF-02 Step 4 -- same four points, same order, carrying G5's and G7's amendments. Diffed the two blocks against each other: they are identical but for WF-02's longer ISSUE_QUEUE parenthetical, which is appropriate since WF-02 Step 4 is TEST-RUNNER's primary home.

G7 (MINOR) -- CLOSED, AND THE THIRD ROUTE IS NOT AN ESCAPE HATCH. This gate's AC6 tested specifically. Route 3 reads 'A demonstrated mechanism outside this branch, stated causally, and evidenced by a MEASUREMENT of the actual mechanism, never by assertion that one probably exists.' Measurement is required, not optional, and the burden is explicitly stated as HIGHER than routes 1 and 2, not lower: 'Route 3 is the one most easily faked, so hold it to its evidence: if you find yourself about to assert route 1 loosely because neither test quite fits, that is route 3 without its measurement, and it is not an attribution.' That sentence closes the exact escape-hatch route this gate was told to check for -- it makes the loose-route-1 move the named failure mode rather than a tolerated one. Both worked examples carry their evidence explicitly rather than their conclusion (orphaned erl.exe: 'the evidence was the enumerated processes and the measured connection count -- not it's probably the environment'; stale rows: 'the queried rows and the demonstrated absent parent'). The filing requirement survives: 'If you can show none of the three, you may not call the failure pre-existing -- report it as unattributed and file it.' Both compressed checklists carry the three-route form plus 'don't stretch (a) to fit'. Routes 1 and 2 are textually unchanged apart from their list terminators. Route 3 supplements; it does not dilute.

DELETION ACCOUNTING (this gate's AC4) -- ALL 19 ACCOUNTED FOR, NONE UNEXPLAINED. `git show 808e2e1 --numstat --format=''` gives 19/3, 32/4, 27/1, 14/5, 20/0, 23/6 across the six owned files (135/19), plus 77/0 for the step-03 handoff. `git show 808e2e1 --format='' -U0 | grep '^-[^-]'` returns exactly 19 lines, each read individually and mapped: (1) test-design-validator.md, 3 lines -- the cheapness clause, required by G1; (2) core-directives, 4 lines -- 1 the Scope-boundary sentence rewrapped for G4's insertion, 2 the 'one of these two things' framing replaced by 'three' for G7, 1 route 2's terminator changed from '.' to '; or' for G7; (3) GIT_MERGE.md, 1 line -- step 5d's bare 'If FAIL:' re-qualified for G3; (4) WF-02, 5 lines -- 3 item 1's two-route text replaced by three-route for G7, 2 item 3's filing text for G5; (5) WF-04, 6 lines -- the prose paragraph replaced by the checklist for G6/G5/G7; (6) WF-03, 0. Every deletion is a rewrite-in-place at a site one of G1-G7 required amending. NO deletion removes a rule, a piece of evidence, or an incident citation, and none is unaccounted for. Cross-checked the other way as well: the 13/14/15 measurement, the PinRebindTest in-the-diff example, the three mutant counts 17/24/11, the both-directions symmetry paragraph, R2's non-fast-forward clause, R4's carve-out and HANDOFF_PROTOCOL 1.1's 'including your own measurement', and R5's on-pin/off-pin probe are all still present verbatim in the current files. Nothing was weakened.

R1 AND R3 AMENDED TEXT RE-CHECKED FOR NEW AMBIGUITY (this gate's AC5). R1 (touched by G4, G5, G7): no contradiction introduced. The three routes are disjoint and jointly non-exhaustive by design, with the residue explicitly routed to 'unattributed -- report it and file it', so the rule is total. The 'known failure is not an attribution' line now sits between the route list and the route-3 explainer, which is slightly odd ordering but changes no meaning. One readability defect, G11, non-gating. R1's compressed forms in WF-02 and WF-04 are now identical to each other and consistent with the canonical text -- I compared all three, and the compressed versions add nothing the canonical does not say. R3 (touched by G1, G2): the role file and WF-03 now say the same thing in the same direction, and the role file's cross-reference names WF-03's section by its exact heading so the pointer resolves. No new ambiguity.

RULING ON THE PR-BODY TEMPLATE (this gate's AC3) -- REAL DEFECT, IN SCOPE NOW, GATING. This is the FAIL; see issue G8 for the full reasoning and the change that closes it.

SCOPE OF THIS STEP. `git status --porcelain` before commit shows only `handoffs/ADHOC-20260821-002/step-04-reviewer-regate.json`. No file outside handoffs/ was modified by me; I did not rewrite any doc. I did not write handoffs/registry.json or handoffs/orchestrator.log (ORCH's). completed_at read from the clock via `date -u`, not from memory.

issues.description: G8 -- GIT_MERGE.md STEP 7's PR BODY TEMPLATE PRINTS A BARE `mix test: PASS`, AND AFTER G3 THAT IS A SANCTIONED FALSE STATEMENT ON THE ONE ARTEFACT A HUMAN READS. This is the item DOC-UPDATER raised as a consequence of its own G3 fix and correctly declined to fix unasked. RULING: it is a real defect, it is caused by this run, and it is in scope NOW rather than as a follow-up. Reasoning, in three parts. (i) CAUSED BY THIS RUN, not merely exposed by it. Before 808e2e1, an agent writing 'PASS' next to 13-15 failures was making an unsanctioned claim reached by the count-matching R1 forbids -- a defect of practice. After 808e2e1, the Precondition and step 5d both officially define green as 'no failure attributable to this branch', so the SAME 'PASS' is now the correct and prescribed label for a run that reported failures. The run converted an agent error into an instructed output. That is a weakening introduced by this pass, and this gate was asked specifically to confirm the rework weakened nothing. (ii) IT IS THE EXACT SHAPE core-directives FORBIDS. 'Never Call a Red Pipeline OK Without a Source' is about not attaching an OK label to a red run without carrying its justification. G3 supplies the justification but parks it in a handoff JSON; step 7 emits the label to the PR with no pointer to it. The asymmetry matters: every other artefact this run touched is read by agents who will follow the pointer, and the PR body is the one artefact read by a human who will not. (iii) NOT A FOLLOW-UP. The change is one template line in a file this run already edited twice, and this gate applied the same standard one iteration ago when it ruled GIT_MERGE.md a required home for R1 (step-02 G3) on a discoverability argument of comparable size; passing a same-file, same-rule completeness item now would be a weaker standard applied to the run's own consequence. Rework budget is 1 of 3. CHANGE THAT CLOSES IT: in GIT_MERGE.md step 7's --body template, replace the line `- mix test: PASS` with a form that cannot be written truthfully without the attribution, e.g. `- mix test: <passed>/<total>, <N> pre-existing failures, each structurally attributed per core-directives.md's Failure Attribution Is Structural (see handoffs/<run-id>/) -- 0 attributable to this branch`, and add one sentence under the template: 'Green here means no failure attributable to this branch (see the Precondition). If the count is non-zero, the PR body must say so and say where the attribution is recorded -- writing a bare PASS next to a non-zero failure count is forbidden by core-directives.md's Never Call a Red Pipeline OK Without a Source.' The `mix compile --warnings-as-errors: PASS` line needs no change: that gate genuinely is zero-tolerance.

G9 -- THE G1 FIX AMENDED THE VALIDATOR'S ROLE FILE BUT NOT THE PRODUCER'S, AND THE VALIDATOR'S NEW MANDATE HAS NO OBJECT IF THE PRODUCER SKIPS. NON-GATING, and the distinction from G1 is deliberate: `.claude/agents/test-designer.md` lines 49-51 contain NO permissive qualifier ('actually verify it rather than asserting it'), state a necessary and not a sufficient condition, and therefore do not CONTRADICT WF-03's rank-3 mandate that 'where the pre-fix failure is non-existence, the fail-first requirement is satisfied ONLY by additionally MUTATING the shipped logic'. Precedence never fires, so the mandate stands -- unlike G1, where a higher-rank file actively overrode it. What remains is discoverability plus one concrete second-order hole worth naming: test-design-validator.md now requires applying 'at least one of TEST-DESIGNER's reported mutants', so if a TEST-DESIGNER that read only its role file reports none, the validator's mandatory clause has an empty set to draw from and a weak model will resolve that as N/A rather than as a FAIL. SUGGESTED (fold into the G8 turn, it is two sentences): append to test-designer.md's WF-03 clause -- 'Where the pre-fix failure is that the code under test did not exist, that check is trivially satisfied and proves nothing; you MUST additionally mutate the shipped logic and record which tests fail for each mutant (WF-03, When the pre-fix failure is the code under test does not exist), reverting each mutant and verifying the revert.' And in test-design-validator.md, state that a WF-03 non-existence case arriving with NO reported mutants is itself a FAIL, so the mandate cannot be voided by an empty set.

G10 -- THE G5 DEFECT SURVIVES IN ONE MORE PLACE: core-directives' Unblock-Everything Scope boundary (the very sentence G4 edited) still tells the discovering agent to 'register it under docs/issues/ISS-NNNN.yaml and, if a gh remote is configured and reachable, file it as a real GitHub issue too'. `docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md` lines 31 and 49-50 forbid exactly that: 'only ORCH calls the queue -- the discovering agent reports the finding, it does not call gh or letflow-queue itself', and ids are allocated atomically. NON-GATING for a precise reason worth recording, because it is the inverse of G1: protocol docs are rank 4 and core-directives is rank 5, so an agent applying Instruction Precedence correctly reaches the RIGHT answer here. The permissive text sits BELOW the strict text rather than above it. It is also pre-existing (b13a523 did not touch it) rather than introduced by this run. Still worth closing while the file is open: add the same deferring clause G5 added to WF-02 -- report the finding to ORCH, which allocates the id and files.

G11 -- G4's insertion is correct in substance but sits awkwardly inside its host sentence, which now carries two consecutive em-dash parentheticals: 'A defect you merely notice while working -- for a test failure, which side of this line it falls on is decided by ... below, not by judgement -- unrelated, not blocking your acceptance criteria -- is filed and forwarded'. The original em-dash pair around 'unrelated, not blocking your acceptance criteria' was the apposition DEFINING 'a defect you merely notice'; the new clause is spliced between the noun and its definition, so a literal reader can mis-scope which parenthetical qualifies what. Meaning is recoverable and no rule changes, hence non-gating. Suggested: make the new clause its own sentence after the host one rather than nesting it -- same words, no re-scoping risk. Consistent with this gate's own step-02 Ruling 2 that mechanical scannability is the standard for weak-model-facing text.

result.next_action: ORCH routes rework iteration 2 (of 3) to DOC-UPDATER for G8 only as the gating item -- one template line plus one sentence in `docs/agents/protocols/GIT_MERGE.md` step 7, which is already in the existing owned_modules, so NO scope widening is needed this time. G9, G10 and G11 are MINOR and non-gating; all three are one- or two-sentence edits in files already in owned_modules (`.claude/agents/test-designer.md` is NOT -- widen for G9 if ORCH elects to fold it in), and folding them into the same turn is cheaper than filing them. If ORCH prefers to close the run now, G8 is the only item that must not be deferred; G9-G11 may instead be reported to the queue per ISSUE_QUEUE.md. Neither b13a523 nor 808e2e1 should be reverted -- G1-G7 are all closed and iteration 2 is additive on top. Re-gate at REVIEWER after the G8 fix; that re-gate is small and should check only that the PR body cannot be written truthfully without carrying the attribution.
